apis.returns: Promise<GPUAdapter|null>. null when WebGPU is present but no usable adapter (blocklisted driver, GPU process crashed, Linux non-Intel in Chrome, software-only). navigator.gpu is undefined when WebGPU is not shipped or the context is not secure (HTTPS required).
apis.support: Chrome/Edge desktop: 113+ on Windows (D3D12), macOS (Metal), ChromeOS; Linux only since Chrome 144 and only Intel Gen12+ GPUs (MDN BCD 8.1.3, 2026-09-24). Chrome Android: 121+ on Android 12+ with Qualcomm Adreno / ARM Mali (Vulkan). Samsung Internet: 25+. Firefox: 141+ Windows only, 145+ Apple Silicon on macOS 26, 147+ Apple Silicon on all supported macOS versions; NOT on Intel Macs, Linux, or Android (Android/Linux targeted for 2026 but not shipped as of Firefox 156). Safari: 26+ on macOS, iOS, iPadOS, visionOS (current Safari/iOS is 27, released 2026-09-14). All iOS/iPadOS browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave on iOS) use WebKit, so they have WebGPU exactly when the OS is iOS/iPadOS 26+. Old browsers: undefined.
apis.caveats: powerPreference 'high-performance' vs 'low-power' only has effect on multi-GPU systems (dual-GPU Intel MacBook Pro, Windows laptops with Optimus/hybrid). Chrome on Windows honours it in recent versions; Safari and Firefox mostly ignore it. Spec says a UA may return the same adapter for both. Always request 'high-performance' for AI. requestAdapter can take 50-500 ms the first time (GPU process start). An adapter can be 'consumed' after requestDevice; request a fresh one if needed. Brave may hide or farble details. Inside a sandboxed iframe WebGPU still works (no permissions-policy gate), but in a hidden/background tab device creation may be delayed.

apis.api: GPUAdapter.info (GPUAdapterInfo: vendor, architecture, device, description, subgroupMinSize, subgroupMaxSize, isFallbackAdapter)
apis.returns: Synchronous object (older Chrome <127 needed adapter.requestAdapterInfo()). Chrome: vendor lower-case ('nvidia','amd','intel','apple','qualcomm','arm','samsung','img-tec','google','microsoft','mesa'), architecture from Dawn gpu_info.json normalised ('lovelace','blackwell','ampere','turing','pascal','rdna-2','rdna-3','gcn-5','gen-9','gen-12lp','xe-lpg','xe-2lpg','xe-3lpg','adreno-6xx','adreno-7xx','adreno-8xx','valhall','bifrost','gen-5' (Mali 5th gen), apple 'metal-3'/'common-3'), device and description are empty strings unless chrome://flags/#enable-webgpu-developer-features. Safari 26+: vendor, architecture, device and description all equal the first word of the Metal device name, lower-cased with non-alphanumerics stripped (WebKit Source/WebCore/Modules/WebGPU/GPUAdapterInfo.h): 'apple' on Apple Silicon Macs, iPhones and iPads; 'intelr' (from 'Intel(R) ...') or 'amd' on Intel Macs. Safari isFallbackAdapter is always false. Firefox: vendor/architecture/device/description are hard-coded empty strings (dom/webgpu/Adapter.h); subgroupMinSize=4, subgroupMaxSize=128 fixed; isFallbackAdapter true only for a CPU adapter (false under resistFingerprinting).
apis.support: Chrome 127+ (info attribute), isFallbackAdapter moved from GPUAdapter to GPUAdapterInfo in Chrome 136 (GPUAdapter.isFallbackAdapter removed in Chrome 140; still on Chrome Android per BCD). subgroupMin/MaxSize: Chrome 134+/144 BCD, Firefox 141 (constant), Safari: preview only. Safari 26+ has info with the stripped-vendor behaviour. Firefox 141+ (Windows/Apple Silicon only) returns empty strings.
apis.caveats: Treat 'architecture' as a generation class, not a SKU: 'lovelace' covers RTX 4060 (8 GB, 272 GB/s) through RTX 4090 (24 GB, 1008 GB/s). Combine with WebGL UNMASKED_RENDERER which in Chrome contains the exact model. Safari's 'apple' vs 'intelr'/'amd' is the single most reliable Apple Silicon vs Intel Mac signal from Safari 26+. Values are not stable across browser versions; parse defensively and lower-case everything.

apis.returns: GPUSupportedLimits with the adapter's ceilings (not the defaults a device gets without requiredLimits). Spec defaults: maxBufferSize 268435456 (256 MiB), maxStorageBufferBindingSize 134217728 (128 MiB), maxComputeWorkgroupStorageSize 16384. Typical adapter values: Chrome desktop discrete/Apple GPUs maxBufferSize 2-4 GiB (often 4294967296 on D3D12/Metal) and maxStorageBufferBindingSize 2-4 GiB minus 4; Chrome Android Adreno/Mali typically 1-2 GiB / 1-2 GiB (varies by driver); maxComputeWorkgroupStorageSize 32768 on almost all desktop and modern mobile GPUs. Safari (WebKit HardwareCapabilities.mm): macOS maxBufferSize = max(min(MTLDevice.maxBufferLength, 1 GiB), min(INT_MAX, maxBufferLength/3)) so usually ~2 GiB (2147483644) on Apple Silicon Macs; iOS/iPadOS maxBufferSize = max(256 MiB, min(1 GiB, maxBufferLength/3)); maxStorageBufferBindingSize = maxBufferSize; maxComputeWorkgroupStorageSize = 32 KiB.
apis.support: Everywhere WebGPU ships. Firefox resets limits to spec defaults when resistFingerprinting (RFPTarget::WebGPULimits) is on.
apis.caveats: These are single-allocation caps, NOT total VRAM; drivers report fixed values unrelated to installed memory, and Chrome may bucket values into tiers for anti-fingerprinting. Use them as GATES: WebLLM/MLC and transformers.js need maxStorageBufferBindingSize >= 1 GiB for normal 7-8B builds (below that only 'low-resource' builds with smaller shards/contexts are usable; below 256 MiB practically only sub-1B models); maxComputeWorkgroupStorageSize >= 32768 is assumed by most tuned matmul kernels (16384 -> slower fallback kernels). On iOS a maxBufferSize of exactly 1 GiB vs 256-512 MiB is a weak RAM-class hint (maxBufferLength scales with device RAM) - low confidence. To use more than defaults you must pass requiredLimits to requestDevice.

apis.support: shader-f16: Chrome 120+ where hardware supports FP16 (Apple M/A-series, NVIDIA Turing+, AMD RDNA, Intel Gen11+/Xe, Adreno 6xx+/Mali Valhall; missing on many older/Pascal-era or some Windows driver combos); Safari 26+ on Apple GPUs; Firefox: exposure depends on wgpu backend - check the set. subgroups: Chrome 134+ (shipped feature 'subgroups'); Safari: Technology Preview only; Firefox: not supported (source TODO bug 1955417). timestamp-query: Chrome (results quantised to 100 microseconds unless developer flag), Safari 26 partial, Firefox varies.
apis.caveats: shader-f16 absence means WebLLM must use q4f32 builds (about 1.3-2x slower and more memory for activations) - downgrade an in-browser 'WELL' by one notch. subgroups speeds up reductions/matmul (~10-30% in llama-style kernels) but is optional. Do not use features as a GPU identifier when info is available.

apis.api: WebGL / WebGL2 WEBGL_debug_renderer_info (UNMASKED_VENDOR_WEBGL 0x9245, UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL 0x9246), MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, getSupportedExtensions
apis.returns: Strings like 'ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (0x00002786) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)'. MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE 4096/8192/16384/32768 (Apple GPUs 16384; desktop discrete 16384-32768; low-end mobile 4096-8192). Extension list (e.g. WEBGL_compressed_texture_astc present on Apple GPUs and most mobile GPUs, absent on Intel/AMD Mac GPUs and desktop Windows GPUs).
apis.support: Chrome/Edge/Samsung: extension available, exact model in renderer (UA reduction did not touch it). Firefox 53+: extension still available but DEPRECATED (bug 1722782, may be removed; already disabled in Nightly), UNMASKED_RENDERER is sanitised into buckets with a ', or similar' suffix since Firefox 91 (bug 1715690), and RENDERER now also returns the sanitised string; disabled entirely with privacy.resistFingerprinting. Safari (macOS and all iOS browsers): vendor 'Apple Inc.', renderer 'Apple GPU' (hard-coded since 2020) - no model info. Works in old browsers (Safari 9.1+, Chrome 33+).
apis.caveats: Always fall back to gl.getParameter(gl.RENDERER) if the extension is missing. Brave farbles/masks. Software renderers ('SwiftShader', 'llvmpipe', 'Microsoft Basic Render Driver', 'ANGLE (Google, Vulkan ... SwiftShader') mean GPU acceleration is off: treat GPU as absent. Creating a WebGL context costs 20-100 ms; release it with WEBGL_lose_context.

apis.returns: Approximate RAM in GiB, rounded to nearest power of two, clamped. Chrome 147+ (shipped April 2026, chromestatus 6330376953921536): desktop/ChromeOS values 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; Android values 1, 2, 4, 8. Before Chrome 147: 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 on all platforms (8 was the cap). Rounding is in log2 space: 3 GB -> 4, 6 GB -> 8, 12 GB -> 16 (desktop) / 8 (Android), 24 GB -> 32, 48/64/128 GB -> 32.
apis.support: Chrome/Edge 63+, Opera, Samsung Internet (Chromium-based, value set follows its Chromium base; Samsung Internet 30 is on an older Chromium so likely still capped at 8). Not in Firefox or Safari (any platform, incl. all iOS browsers). HTTPS only.
apis.caveats: 32 means 'about 24 GB or more' - cannot distinguish 32/64/128 GB workstations; ask the user when 32. Android 8 means 'about 6 GB or more' (6, 8, 12, 16, 24 GB phones all report 8) - use userAgentData model lookup to refine. Parse the Chrome major version to know which bucket scheme applies. Brave may farble. Also available as Sec-CH-Device-Memory client hint (irrelevant for a static single file).

apis.support: Chrome/Edge/Samsung/Firefox: true logical core count (Apple M4 Pro -> 12 or 14; Ryzen 9 7950X -> 32; Snapdragon 8 Elite -> 8). Safari 15.4+ (macOS and iOS): clamped to 4 or 8 (webkit bug 233381) - 8 on basically every modern iPhone/Mac. Firefox with resistFingerprinting reports 2 (and newer Firefox fingerprinting protections in private/strict mode may also coarsen). Old browsers: undefined.
apis.caveats: Logical cores include hyper-threads and efficiency cores; CPU inference speed is bandwidth-bound anyway, so use cores mainly to size WASM thread pools (threads = min(cores, 8) typically best; beyond ~8 threads decode speed saturates memory bandwidth). A value >= 16 on desktop strongly implies a desktop-class CPU (8+ P-cores).

apis.returns: Low entropy: {brands:[{brand,version}], mobile:bool, platform:'Windows'|'macOS'|'Android'|'Chrome OS'|'Linux'}. High entropy promise: architecture 'x86'|'arm', bitness '64'|'32', model (Android only, e.g. 'Pixel 9 Pro', 'SM-S938B'; empty on desktop), platformVersion (Windows: '15.0.0'+ = Windows 11 when major >= 13, '10.0.0' and below = Windows 10; macOS e.g. '26.0.0'; Android e.g. '16.0.0'), formFactors array e.g. ['Desktop'], ['Mobile'], ['Tablet'], ['XR'], ['EInk'], ['Watch'], ['Automotive'], wow64 bool.
apis.support: Chrome/Edge/Opera 90+ (formFactors ~Chrome 116+), Samsung Internet 23+ (getHighEntropyValues). Not in Firefox or Safari. Chrome 144+: high-entropy values in iframes controlled by the ch-ua-high-entropy-values permissions policy (default allows, but a hosting page can deny; values then come back empty).
apis.caveats: This is the only way in Chromium to get CPU architecture after UA reduction (reduced UA always says 'Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7' and 'Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64'). On an Apple Silicon Mac, Chrome reports architecture 'arm'; Intel Mac 'x86'. On Windows on ARM (Snapdragon X Elite) 'arm'. Wrap in try/catch; can reject with NotAllowedError.

apis.returns: {quota, usage} in bytes. Chrome/Edge: quota ~60% of total disk per origin (so totalDisk ~= quota/0.6); incognito much smaller. Firefox: best-effort limit about 10% of disk or 10 GiB per eTLD+1 group, 50% of disk when persisted. Safari 17+: origin quota up to ~60% of disk for browser apps (lower for web views), with eviction after 7 days of no interaction for non-installed sites.
apis.support: Chrome 61+, Firefox 57+, Safari 17+ (macOS and iOS), Samsung 8+. Absent in older Safari.
apis.caveats: Needed to tell whether an in-browser model (1-5 GB shards in Cache Storage / OPFS) can be cached. Throws SecurityError in sandboxed iframes without allow-same-origin. The quota is not free space. Do not rely on it as a precise disk-size probe (values rounded / capped).

apis.returns: Bytes. jsHeapSizeLimit is a build/config constant, NOT device RAM: typically 4294705152 (~4 GiB) on 64-bit desktop Chrome, ~2172649472 (~2 GiB) on 32-bit builds and many Android devices, lower on low-RAM Android.
apis.support: Chromium only (Chrome, Edge, Samsung, Opera). Non-standard, deprecated. Replacement performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory() requires crossOriginIsolated.
apis.caveats: Useful only as a 64-bit vs 32-bit hint and for a low-RAM Android signal; values quantised unless --enable-precise-memory-info.

apis.api: WebAssembly feature detection (SIMD, threads, relaxed-SIMD, memory64) via WebAssembly.validate
apis.support: Fixed-width SIMD: Chrome 91, Firefox 89, Safari 16.4 (macOS+iOS). Threads/atomics: Chrome 74 (Android 88), Firefox 79, Safari 15.2 - but only usable when crossOriginIsolated (SharedArrayBuffer). Relaxed SIMD: Chrome 114, Firefox 146, Safari: Technology Preview only (not in Safari 27). Memory64: Chrome 133, Firefox 134, Safari: preview only. JSPI: Chrome 137, Firefox 153, Safari 27. (MDN BCD 8.1.3.)
apis.caveats: Without SIMD, WASM CPU inference is ~2-4x slower: treat in-browser CPU LLMs above ~0.5B as NO. Without threads, WASM runs single-threaded: roughly 3-6x slower prefill vs 4-8 threads. Memory32 caps a WASM heap at 4 GiB (2 GiB in some Safari builds/iOS realistically ~1-1.5 GiB before jetsam), so CPU-path in-browser models are limited to ~2-3 GB weights even on big machines; memory64 lifts this (Chrome/Firefox only). Byte sequences below are the standard wasm-feature-detect modules; verified to validate in V8 (Node 22).

apis.returns: crossOriginIsolated true only when the document is served with Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (or credentialless in Chromium/Firefox). SharedArrayBuffer constructor is exposed only then (Chrome desktop 92+, Firefox 79+, Safari 15.2+).
apis.support: All modern browsers; undefined in old ones.
apis.caveats: A single-file page hosted where you cannot set headers (e.g. inside an artifact iframe or a file:// open) will NOT be cross-origin isolated, so WASM threads, high-resolution timers (5 microseconds) and measureUserAgentSpecificMemory are unavailable. Workaround coi-serviceworker requires a same-origin service worker - usually impossible in a sandboxed host. Design the benchmark to be single-threaded and to tolerate 100 microsecond - 1 ms timer resolution.
apis.code: var coi = (typeof self !== 'undefined' && self.crossOriginIsolated === true); var sab = (typeof SharedArrayBuffer === 'function');

apis.returns: CSS pixel (point) dimensions; dpr 1/1.5/2/2.625/3 etc.; maxTouchPoints 0 on Mac, 5 on iPhone/iPad; navigator.platform 'iPhone', 'iPad' (old), 'MacIntel' (all Macs incl. Apple Silicon, AND iPadOS 13+ in desktop mode), 'Win32', 'Linux armv8l'/'Linux aarch64' (Android), 'Linux x86_64'.
apis.caveats: Screen size changes with orientation (use min/max), iOS Display Zoom (e.g. a 393x852 iPhone shows 320x693 or 375x812-ish 'zoomed' sizes), external monitors, and browser zoom does not change screen.* but does change devicePixelRatio in Chromium desktop. Firefox resistFingerprinting reports window size as screen size. navigator.platform is frozen/legacy but still the practical iPad detector: platform==='MacIntel' && maxTouchPoints>1 => iPad.

apis.api: navigator.connection (NetworkInformation: effectiveType, downlink, rtt, saveData, type)
apis.returns: effectiveType 'slow-2g'|'2g'|'3g'|'4g'; downlink in Mbps rounded to 25 kbps and capped at 10; rtt rounded to 25 ms; saveData bool; type ('wifi','cellular', Android only).
apis.support: Chrome/Edge/Samsung/Opera desktop and Android. Not Safari (any), not Firefox (removed; Firefox Android had it until 98).
apis.caveats: Only use to warn about download time (e.g. 'a 4.9 GB model at ~10 Mbps = 65 min'); downlink cap of 10 Mbps makes it useless above that. Respect saveData by not auto-running large benchmarks.
apis.code:
var c = navigator.connection || navigator.mozConnection || navigator.webkitConnection || null;
var net = c ? { eff: c.effectiveType || '', down: c.downlink || 0, save: !!c.saveData, type: c.type || '' } : null;

apis.support: Chrome/Edge/Samsung desktop and Android. Removed from Firefox in 52; never in Safari. Restricted to top-level and same-origin frames by the 'battery' permissions policy (default 'self') since Chrome 103 - rejects in cross-origin iframes.
apis.caveats: Laptops on battery (Windows power plans, macOS Low Power Mode) and phones below ~20% or hot will throttle; benchmark results can be 30-60% lower. Show 'plug in for accurate results' when charging===false.

apis.returns: (pointer: coarse)/(hover: none) => touch-first phone/tablet; (color-gamut: p3) and (dynamic-range: high) => modern high-end display (all Apple devices since ~2016, flagship Android); (prefers-reduced-motion), (prefers-color-scheme) for UI; (display-mode: standalone) => installed PWA.
apis.support: Universal in modern browsers; dynamic-range Chrome 98+/Safari 13.1+/Firefox 100+.
apis.caveats: Weak hints only; use for phone vs desktop form factor where userAgentData is absent (Firefox/Safari). A Windows touchscreen laptop reports (any-pointer: coarse) but (pointer: fine).
apis.code:
function mq(q){ try { return window.matchMedia(q).matches; } catch(e){ return false; } }
var formHints = { coarse: mq('(pointer: coarse)'), noHover: mq('(hover: none)'), p3: mq('(color-gamut: p3)'), hdr: mq('(dynamic-range: high)') };

apis.api: Chrome built-in AI (LanguageModel.availability()) and WebNN (navigator.ml) - optional extra signals
apis.support: Chrome desktop only (Windows/macOS/Linux/ChromeOS); Gemini Nano requires roughly >4 GB VRAM GPU or >=16 GB RAM with >=4 cores and ~22 GB free disk; web-page exposure has been via origin trial/flags and extensions - treat as optional. WebNN: behind flag / origin trial in Chromium; not in Safari/Firefox stable.
apis.caveats: If LanguageModel.availability() returns anything other than 'unavailable' it is an independent Google-confirmed hint that the machine meets Gemini Nano hardware bars (~16 GB RAM class or 4 GB+ VRAM). Never block on it.

renderer_string_formats: Chrome/Edge Windows NVIDIA (ANGLE D3D11): 'ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (0x00002786) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)'. Parse: /ANGLE \(([^,]+), (.+?)(?: \(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+\))? Direct3D/ -> vendor, model. Hex is PCI device id (useful to disambiguate laptop vs desktop SKUs, e.g. 0x2786 = RTX 4070 desktop, 0x2820 = RTX 4070 Laptop). Laptop GPUs contain 'Laptop GPU'.

Chrome/Edge Windows AMD: 'ANGLE (AMD, AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (0x0000744C) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)'; AMD APU: 'ANGLE (AMD, AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (0x000015BF) Direct3D11 ...)' (generic name - use PCI id: 0x15BF/0x15C8 = Phoenix 780M/760M, 0x1586 = Strix Halo 8060S, 0x150E = Strix Point 890M).

Chrome/Edge Windows Intel: 'ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 (0x00005917) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)', 'ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) Arc(TM) 140V GPU (16GB) (0x000064A0) Direct3D11 ...)' (Lunar Lake - note the '(16GB)'/'(32GB)' suffix reveals system RAM!), 'ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (0x00009A49) ...)'. Windows on ARM: 'ANGLE (Qualcomm, Qualcomm(R) Adreno(TM) X1-85 GPU (0x...) Direct3D11 ...)'.

Chrome/Edge Windows software fallback: 'ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)' or 'ANGLE (Microsoft, Microsoft Basic Render Driver Direct3D11 ...)' => no usable GPU (RDP/VM/blocklisted driver). WebGPU info then vendor 'google'/'microsoft' architecture 'swiftshader'/'warp' and isFallbackAdapter true.

Chrome/Edge macOS Apple Silicon: 'ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M3 Pro, Unspecified Version)' - exact chip tier (M1..M5, base/Pro/Max/Ultra) is present: parse /Apple (M\d+)(?: (Pro|Max|Ultra))?/. WebGPU adapter.info: {vendor:'apple', architecture:'metal-3' (Dawn may report 'common-3'), device:'', description:''}.

Chrome/Edge macOS Intel: 'ANGLE (Intel Inc., Intel(R) Iris(TM) Plus Graphics 655, OpenGL 4.1)' or Metal backend 'ANGLE (Intel, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630, Unspecified Version)'; dual-GPU MBP: 'ANGLE (ATI Technologies Inc., AMD Radeon Pro 5500M OpenGL Engine, OpenGL 4.1)' or '... ANGLE Metal Renderer: AMD Radeon Pro 5500M ...'.

Chrome Linux: 'ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080/PCIe/SSE2, OpenGL 4.5.0 NVIDIA 550.xx)', 'ANGLE (Intel, Mesa Intel(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2), OpenGL 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 24.x)', 'ANGLE (AMD, AMD Radeon RX 6800 (radeonsi, navi21, LLVM 17...), OpenGL 4.6 ...)'. 'llvmpipe' => software.

Chrome/Samsung Internet Android: 'ANGLE (Qualcomm, Adreno (TM) 750, OpenGL ES 3.2)' (older builds: plain 'Adreno (TM) 750', vendor 'Qualcomm'); Mali: 'ANGLE (ARM, Mali-G715-Immortalis MC11, OpenGL ES 3.2)' or 'Mali-G78'; Samsung Exynos RDNA: 'ANGLE (Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., ANGLE Vulkan ... Samsung Xclipse 940 ...)' / 'Xclipse 950'; Google Tensor G5 uses Imagination 'PowerVR D-Series DXT-48-1536'; low-end 'PowerVR Rogue GE8320'. WebGPU info: {vendor:'qualcomm', architecture:'adreno-7xx'|'adreno-8xx'} or {vendor:'arm', architecture:'valhall'|'gen-5'} or {vendor:'samsung', architecture:'rdna-2'|'rdna-3'}. Map Adreno number to SoC: 830 = Snapdragon 8 Elite, 840 = 8 Elite Gen 5, 750 = 8 Gen 3, 740 = 8 Gen 2, 730 = 8 Gen 1, 7xx-lower = 7-series, 6xx = older/mid.

Firefox (all desktop OSes and Android): sanitised bucket with suffix ', or similar': 'ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0), or similar', 'ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) HD Graphics 400 Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0), or similar', 'Apple M1, or similar' (bucket for all Apple Silicon), 'Adreno (TM) 640, or similar', 'Mali-G51, or similar'. Strip /, or similar$/ and treat model as a generation class only (a 4090 may show as a bucket like 'GTX 980'). Firefox WebGPU adapter.info fields are all ''. With resistFingerprinting: extension unavailable and RENDERER = 'Mozilla'.

Safari macOS, iOS, iPadOS (and every iOS browser, since all are WebKit): UNMASKED_VENDOR 'Apple Inc.', UNMASKED_RENDERER 'Apple GPU' (hard-coded, no model). Safari 26+ WebGPU adapter.info: vendor = architecture = device = description = 'apple' on Apple Silicon Mac/iPhone/iPad; on Intel Macs the first word of the Metal device name normalised, i.e. 'intelr' ('Intel(R) ...') or 'amd'.
Brave: returns realistic but farbled/randomised strings per site/session and may block WebGPU info; detect Brave via navigator.brave && navigator.brave.isBrave() and lower confidence.
platform_inference:
Decision tree (evaluate in order, record confidence for each conclusion):

1) OS/form factor. Chromium: userAgentData.platform + getHighEntropyValues (platformVersion, formFactors, architecture, model). Others: UA string. iPadOS 13+ Safari/any iOS browser in desktop mode reports 'Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7' and navigator.platform 'MacIntel' -> iPad if navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1 (Macs report 0). iPhone: /iPhone/ in UA. ChromeOS: 'CrOS' in UA / platform 'Chrome OS' (Chromebook Plus = 8 GB+ RAM, most others 4-8 GB). Windows 11 vs 10: platformVersion major >= 13 = Win11 (UA always says NT 10.0). Android version from UA is frozen at 'Android 10; K' in reduced UA - use platformVersion.

2) Apple Silicon vs Intel Mac (all browsers say 'Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7'):
 - Chrome/Edge/Opera/Brave: getHighEntropyValues(['architecture']) -> 'arm' = Apple Silicon (high confidence); also WebGL renderer contains 'Apple M<n>' with exact tier.
 - Firefox: WebGL renderer 'Apple M1, or similar' vs 'Intel ... or similar'/'AMD ...'; also Firefox exposes navigator.gpu on Apple Silicon (147+) but NOT on Intel Macs - presence of navigator.gpu in Firefox on macOS => Apple Silicon.
 - Safari 26+: navigator.gpu present on both, adapter.info.vendor === 'apple' => Apple Silicon; 'intelr'/'amd' => Intel (high confidence, from WebKit source). Safari < 26: WebGL extension heuristic - Apple GPUs expose WEBGL_compressed_texture_astc (and typically lack WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc_srgb), Intel/AMD Mac GPUs expose S3TC but not ASTC (medium confidence). Also macOS 26 'Tahoe' is the last Intel release; Safari 27 on macOS 27 => Apple Silicon.
 - Screen hint (Macs): 1512x982 (MBP 14 default), 1728x1117 (MBP 16), 1470x956 (MBA 13 M2+), 1710x1112 (MBA 15) are notched Apple-Silicon-only panels; 1440x900/1536x960/1680x1050/1792x1120 are ambiguous (Intel MBP or M1 MBA/MBP13). Low-medium confidence (user may change scaling).
 - Which M chip in Safari/Firefox: not exposed -> ask the user (dropdown: M1..M5 x base/Pro/Max/Ultra, RAM 8/16/18/24/32/36/48/64/96/128/192/256/512) and/or classify by WebGPU bandwidth benchmark: <130 GB/s measured-peak => base M1-M5 (68/100/100/120/153 GB/s), 130-300 => Pro (M1/M2 Pro 200, M3 Pro 150, M4 Pro 273), 300-600 => Max (M1/M2 Max 400, M3 Max 300/400, M4 Max 410/546), >600 => Ultra (800/819). Mac RAM is never exposed outside Chrome's deviceMemory (8/16/32 buckets) - always ask; default assumption if unanswered: base chip 16 GB (Apple's minimum since late 2024), Pro 24 GB, Max 36-48 GB.

3) iPhone model / RAM class (Safari gives 'Apple GPU', hardwareConcurrency clamped, no deviceMemory). Use screen short x long side in points + dpr (portrait), then iOS version from UA ('OS 26_0' / Safari 'Version/27.0'; iOS 26 requires iPhone 11/A13 or newer; iOS 27 drops more). Table (points, dpr -> models -> RAM):
 - 320x568 @2 -> SE 1st gen/5s -> 1-2 GB (NO for everything but tiny models).
 - 375x667 @2 -> 6/6s/7/8/SE2/SE3 -> 2-4 GB (SE3 = 4 GB, A15).
 - 414x736 @3 -> 6+/7+/8 Plus -> 3 GB.
 - 375x812 @3 -> X/XS/11 Pro/12 mini/13 mini -> 3-4 GB.
 - 414x896 @2 -> XR/11 -> 3-4 GB; @3 -> XS Max/11 Pro Max -> 4 GB.
 - 390x844 @3 -> 12/12 Pro/13/13 Pro/14/16e -> 4 GB (12, 13), 6 GB (12 Pro, 13 Pro, 14), 8 GB (16e, A18).
 - 428x926 @3 -> 12 Pro Max/13 Pro Max/14 Plus -> 6 GB.
 - 393x852 @3 -> 14 Pro/15/15 Pro/16 -> 6 GB (14 Pro, 15), 8 GB (15 Pro, 16).
 - 430x932 @3 -> 14 Pro Max/15 Plus/15 Pro Max/16 Plus -> 6 GB or 8 GB.
 - 402x874 @3 -> 16 Pro (8 GB), 17 (8 GB), 17 Pro (12 GB), 18 Pro (12 GB, A20 Pro, Sept 2026).
 - 440x956 @3 -> 16 Pro Max (8 GB), 17 Pro Max (12 GB), 18 Pro Max (12 GB).
 - 420x912 @3 -> iPhone Air (12 GB).
 Ambiguous buckets (393x852, 430x932, 402x874, 440x956) -> resolve with a 1-2 s WebGPU compute benchmark (A16 ~1.8 TFLOPS FP32, A17 Pro/A18 ~2.1-2.3, A19 Pro/A20 Pro ~2.5-3+) or ask 'Which iPhone?'. Rule: report RAM as a range and use the LOWER bound for WELL/SLOW verdicts, upper bound for NO. Display Zoom changes points (e.g. 402-wide phone shows 375x812-like values) - if dpr=3 and size maps to a model older than the iOS version supports, suspect zoom. Apple Intelligence-capable (8 GB+) = 15 Pro and newer.
 iPad: MacIntel + touch. Screen sizes: 744x1133 (mini 6/7: 4/8 GB), 820x1180 (Air 4/5, iPad 10: 4-8 GB), 834x1194 (Pro 11 2018-2022, 6-8 GB+; Pro 11 M4/M5 834x1210), 1024x1366 (Pro 12.9, 13-inch Air/Pro 1032x1376 on M4/M5). M-series iPads: 8 GB (16 GB on 1 TB+ storage Pro). Ask when unsure.

4) Android RAM/SoC: Chrome 147+ deviceMemory 1/2/4/8 (8 = >=~6 GB). Refine with getHighEntropyValues(['model']) (Chrome and Samsung Internet 23+) against a lookup table of top models (e.g. SM-S93x = Galaxy S25 family 12 GB, SM-S92x = S24 family 8-12 GB, 'Pixel 9 Pro' 16 GB, 'Pixel 10 Pro' 16 GB, 'Pixel 9'/'Pixel 10' 12 GB), plus GPU from WebGL/WebGPU (Adreno 830/840 = Snapdragon 8 Elite class, 76-85 GB/s LPDDR5X; Adreno 750 = 8 Gen 3; Immortalis-G925 = Dimensity 9400). Firefox Android: no deviceMemory, no userAgentData, no WebGPU - only WebGL renderer (sanitised) + screen -> ask the user for RAM. Usable RAM for a native app on Android ~ 50-60% of total; in-browser tab ~ 25-40%.

5) Windows/Linux PCs: GPU model from WebGL renderer (Chrome exact, Firefox bucketed). VRAM from a lookup table keyed by model string (RTX 4090 24 GB, 4080 16, 4070 Ti 12, 4070 12, 4060 Ti 8/16, 4060 8, 3090 24, 3080 10/12, 3070 8, 3060 12, 5090 32, 5080 16, 5070 Ti 16, 5070 12, 5060 Ti 8/16, RX 7900 XTX 24, 7900 XT 20, 7800 XT 16, 9070 XT 16, Arc B580 12, A770 16...); ambiguous (4060 Ti 8 vs 16, 5060 Ti 8 vs 16) -> ask or assume lower. System RAM: Chrome 147+ deviceMemory 8/16/32 (32 = 24 GB+ -> ask). Integrated GPUs share system RAM (Intel Arc 140V string includes '(16GB)'/'(32GB)'). Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S) = 64-128 GB unified, 256 GB/s. CPU memory bandwidth: assume dual-channel DDR4-3200 51 GB/s (older desktops/laptops), DDR5-5600 90 GB/s, LPDDR5X-8533 (Lunar Lake 136 GB/s, Snapdragon X 135 GB/s).

6) Unknown handling: every inferred field carries {value, source, confidence: high|medium|low}. When RAM or chip tier is low-confidence, show an inline 'Refine' control (chip/RAM/VRAM dropdowns) and recompute; persist the answer in localStorage (try/catch). Never output NO based solely on a missing signal - output 'Unknown - tell us your RAM' instead. Default priors if user skips: desktop Windows 16 GB RAM + detected GPU; Mac 16 GB; iPhone lower bound of bucket; Android 8 GB if deviceMemory==8 else the reported value.
estimation_method:
Two separate verdicts per model: (A) NATIVE (Ollama/llama.cpp/LM Studio/MLX) using the full device, and (B) IN-BROWSER (WebLLM/transformers.js) constrained by the browser. The browser is only a sensor for (A).

1. Memory fit (hard gate).
 weights_GB = total_params_B x bits_per_weight / 8 (Q4_K_M ~4.8-4.9 bpw effective, Q8_0 8.5, FP16 16, MXFP4 ~4.25, MLX 4-bit ~4.5 incl. scales).
 kv_GB = 2 x n_layers x n_kv_heads x head_dim x ctx x bytes (2 for f16) / 1e9. Rule of thumb for GQA 7-9B models: ~0.12-0.15 GB per 1k tokens f16; 70B: ~0.33 GB/1k. Default ctx 8192 (4096 on phones/in-browser).
 need_GB = (weights_GB + kv_GB) x 1.1 + runtime_overhead (0.5 GB native, 0.3 GB WebLLM).
 usable memory:
 - Discrete GPU: VRAM x 0.9 (minus ~0.5-1 GB used by desktop compositor).
 - Apple Silicon native: GPU working set = RAM x 0.67 for <=16 GB... practically Metal recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize ~ 66-75% of RAM (e.g. 16 GB -> ~10.7 GB, 32 GB -> ~21-24 GB, 64 GB -> ~48 GB, 128 GB -> ~96 GB); leave ~4 GB for OS.
 - PC CPU/iGPU native: RAM x 0.7 - 2 GB.
 - iPhone/iPad native app: ~50-60% of RAM (8 GB phone -> ~4-5 GB model budget; 12 GB -> ~6-7 GB). Android native: ~50-60%.
 - In-browser WebGPU: desktop min(usable_native, ~0.5 x RAM) and each tensor must fit maxStorageBufferBindingSize; iOS Safari tab ~ min(0.35 x RAM, 4 GB) before jetsam kills it (low confidence; test); Android Chrome tab ~0.3 x RAM. In-browser WASM CPU: <= ~3.5 GB heap (memory32; 4 GB hard cap), ~1.5 GB practical on iOS.
 If need > usable_fast but <= usable_fast + usable_system (partial offload) -> candidate SLOW; if need > all memory (RAM+VRAM - 4 GB) -> NO.

2. Decode speed (memory-bandwidth bound).
 bytes_per_token = active_params_B x bpw/8 (GB) + kv_read (kv_GB at the current context, ~ignored at short ctx).
 tok/s = eff x BW_GBps / bytes_per_token.
 Efficiency factors (fraction of theoretical peak achieved): CUDA llama.cpp/exllama 0.70-0.80; Metal llama.cpp/MLX 0.65-0.75; Vulkan/ROCm 0.55-0.70; CPU llama.cpp (all cores, AVX2/NEON) 0.50-0.65 of DRAM BW; phones native (MLC/llama.cpp) 0.40-0.55 (thermal throttling after ~1-2 min drops a further 20-40%); WebGPU WebLLM 0.45-0.65 (claims up to ~80% of native on Apple); transformers.js WebGPU 0.30-0.50; WASM SIMD multithread 0.25-0.40; WASM single-thread: compute-bound, ~2-8 tok/s for 0.5B Q4 on a modern desktop core. Use the middle of the range for the estimate, lower bound for the verdict.
 Worked checks: RTX 4090 (1008 GB/s) Llama-3.1-8B Q4_K_M (4.9 GB): 0.75x1008/4.9 = 154 tok/s (measured ~130-150). M2 (100 GB/s) 8B Q4: 0.7x100/4.9 = 14 tok/s (measured ~12-15). M4 Max 546 GB/s, 70B Q4 (~42 GB): 0.7x546/42 = 9 tok/s (measured ~8-10). DDR5-5600 dual channel (90 GB/s) CPU 8B Q4: 0.55x90/4.9 = 10 tok/s. iPhone 16 Pro (~60 GB/s) 3B Q4 (1.9 GB): 0.45x60/1.9 = 14 tok/s.
 MoE: bytes_per_token uses ACTIVE params (gpt-oss-20b: 3.6B active, file ~13 GB, so ~2 GB/token; gpt-oss-120b: 5.1B active, ~61-65 GB; Qwen3-30B-A3B: 3.3B active, Q4 ~18.6 GB), memory fit uses TOTAL params. Add ~15% overhead for router/expert gather. MoE is why 30B-A3B runs WELL on a 32 GB Mac/CPU box.
 Partial offload: t_token = bytes_gpu/(eff_gpu x BW_gpu) + bytes_cpu/(eff_cpu x BW_cpu); tok/s = 1/t. The CPU term dominates quickly (e.g. 24 GB of a 42 GB 70B model on a 4090, rest on 90 GB/s DDR5: 24/756 + 18/50 = 0.032+0.36 s -> ~2.6 tok/s = SLOW). For MoE with experts on CPU (llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe), put attention/shared weights on GPU and only active expert bytes on CPU.
 CPU-only native: BW = DRAM BW (dual-channel DDR4-3200 51, DDR5-5600 90, LPDDR5X-8533 136, Apple M = unified BW but CPU cluster can pull only ~60-90% of it on base chips).
 Prefill / time-to-first-token (compute bound): prefill tok/s = eff_c x FLOPS / (2 x active_params); eff_c 0.3-0.6 GPU, 0.1-0.3 WebGPU without subgroups/f16, CPU uses GFLOPS measured by benchmark. Flag SLOW if a 1,000-token prompt takes > 10 s.

3. Thresholds (LLMs).
 WELL: fits in fast memory with >= 15% headroom AND decode >= 10 tok/s (comfortable reading speed; people read ~4-6 words/s ~ 5-8 tok/s, so 10 gives margin for thinking-model reasoning tokens) AND 1k-token prefill <= 5 s. For reasoning models (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1 distills, gpt-oss) require >= 15 tok/s for WELL because they emit hundreds-thousands of thinking tokens.
 SLOW: fits (possibly with offload/mmap) and 2 <= tok/s < 10, or prefill 5-30 s. Usable for batch/async use.
 NO: does not fit in RAM+VRAM (or browser limit for in-browser), or < 2 tok/s (a 300-token answer takes > 2.5 min), or required runtime absent (no WebGPU and no WASM SIMD for in-browser).
 Show 'borderline' when estimate is within +-25% of a threshold and confidence is not high.

4. Diffusion / image models (compute bound).
 sec_per_image = steps x CFG_passes x TFLOP_per_step / (eff x device_TFLOPS_fp16) + VAE decode.
 Approximate per-step cost at native res (one UNet/DiT pass): SD 1.5 @512^2 ~0.4 TFLOP... use empirical anchors instead: SD1.5 512^2 20 steps: RTX 4090 ~1 s, RTX 3060 ~3-4 s, M2 ~15 s, M1 8 GB ~25-40 s. SDXL 1024^2 25-30 steps: RTX 4090 ~4-5 s, 4070 ~10 s, 3060 12 GB ~20 s, M3 Max ~25-35 s, M2 base ~90-150 s. FLUX.1 [dev]/[schnell] 12B (FP8 ~12 GB, GGUF Q4 ~7 GB) 1024^2: 4090 ~15-20 s for 20-28 steps (schnell 4 steps ~3 s), M3 Max ~90-120 s. Scale anchors by FP16 throughput ratio (TFLOPS: 4090 ~165 dense tensor FP16, 4070 ~58, 3060 ~51, M1 2.6 FP32/~5 FP16, M2 3.6/7, M3 Max ~14/28, M4 Max ~17/34, A17 Pro ~2.1/4.2). Memory: SD1.5 ~2.5 GB, SDXL ~7-8 GB fp16 (6 GB with tiling), SD3.5 Medium ~6-10 GB, FLUX 12B needs >= 12 GB VRAM (Q4 GGUF fits 8 GB with offload).
 Thresholds: WELL <= 30 s per standard image; SLOW 30 s - 5 min; NO > 5 min or does not fit. In-browser diffusion (WebGPU SD-Turbo/SDXL-Turbo via ONNX/transformers.js): only on >= 8 GB GPUs/Apple M-series; multiply native time by 2-3.

5. Speech (Whisper family) - encoder compute bound, decoder bandwidth bound.
 Sizes (fp16 / ggml q5): tiny 39M (75 MB), base 74M (142 MB), small 244M (466 MB), medium 769M (1.5 GB), large-v3 1.55B (3.1 GB fp16, ~1.1 GB q5), large-v3-turbo 809M (1.6 GB fp16, ~0.55 GB q5). Encoder per 30 s window ~ 2 x encoder_params x 1500 frames FLOPs (large: ~2 x 0.64B x 1500 ~ 1.9 TFLOP); decoder ~ bandwidth-bound per token (~50-100 tokens per 30 s).
 Real-time factor RTF = audio_seconds / processing_seconds. WELL >= 3x real-time (live dictation possible); SLOW 0.5x-3x; NO < 0.5x or does not fit. Anchors: whisper.cpp large-v3-turbo on M1/M2 base: ~5-10x RT; on 8-core desktop CPU AVX2: ~1-3x; tiny/base on any 2020+ phone >10x RT. In-browser (transformers.js WebGPU) whisper-base/small WELL on most WebGPU devices; large-v3-turbo WELL on M-series/discrete GPUs, SLOW on phones; WASM-only: tiny/base only.

6. Confidence: combine field confidences - HIGH when GPU model and memory size are both from high-confidence sources (e.g. Chrome renderer 'RTX 4070' + deviceMemory 16), MEDIUM when one is inferred from a bucket/table, LOW when either is a default prior. Let the benchmark override the bandwidth prior when |measured - prior|/prior > 40% (thermal, power-saver, wrong guess).
benchmarks:
Goal: < 5 s total, never freeze the tab, run only after an explicit 'Run quick test' click (also required for user gesture/visibility), and show progress. Order: WebGPU tests first (most informative), then CPU; abort any stage that exceeds its budget.

A) CPU / WASM (single-threaded, since the page is usually not crossOriginIsolated):
 1. Memory bandwidth (JS/TypedArray memcpy): allocate src/dst Float64Array of 32 MiB each (64 MiB if deviceMemory >= 8 or unknown desktop; 16 MiB on phones) - larger than LLC so it hits DRAM. Warm up 2 copies (dst.set(src)), then loop dst.set(src) until >= 250 ms elapsed. GB/s = 2 x bytes x iterations / seconds (read + write). Typical single-thread results: Apple M1-M4 40-100 GB/s (Apple cores pull a lot), desktop x86 DDR5 15-30 GB/s, DDR4 laptop 8-18 GB/s, flagship phone 15-35 GB/s, budget phone 4-10 GB/s. It under-reports aggregate DRAM BW on x86 (one core cannot saturate), so use it as a class check: aggregate_BW_est = single x (2.5 on x86 desktop, 1.3 on Apple, 1.8 on Android).
 2. Compute (WASM SIMD if available, else JS): a 128x128 f32 matmul or an unrolled f32x4 FMA loop compiled from a tiny inline WASM module; run until >= 300 ms; GFLOPS = 2 x N^3 x reps / s. Expected single-core: 20-60 GFLOPS with SIMD on modern desktop/Apple, 5-15 GFLOPS on phones, 1-4 GFLOPS JS without SIMD. Multiply by min(cores, 8) x 0.7 for multithread native estimate.
 Keep each loop in chunks of <= 50 ms and yield (await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))) between chunks so the UI stays responsive; Safari/iOS kills pages that block the main thread > ~5-10 s and may jetsam large allocations - free arrays (set to null) immediately.

B) WebGPU (requestDevice with requiredLimits.maxBufferSize/maxStorageBufferBindingSize = min(adapter limit, 256 MiB)):
 1. Bandwidth: buffer size S = min(256 MiB, adapter.limits.maxBufferSize, maxStorageBufferBindingSize) (64 MiB on phones). Either (a) copyBufferToBuffer src->dst, or better (b) a compute shader that reads vec4<f32> from a storage buffer and writes to another (workgroup_size 256, each invocation strides over 4-8 vec4s). Warm up 2 dispatches (the first includes pipeline compilation, 20-300 ms). Then submit K dispatches in one command encoder (K chosen so estimated GPU time ~100-200 ms: start with K=4, double while total < 150 ms) and await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone(). Repeat 3 times, take the best. GB/s = 2 x S x K / s. Expected (70-90% of peak): RTX 4090 750-900, RTX 4070 380-450, RTX 3060 280-330, M1 55-60, M2 80-90, M3 Pro 120-135, M1/M2 Max 330-370, M4 Max 450-500, Intel Iris Xe 40-60, Lunar Lake 90-110, iPhone 15 Pro/16 Pro 40-55, Adreno 750/830 45-65, Mali mid-range 15-25.
 2. Compute: a WGSL kernel where each invocation runs 256-1024 iterations of 4 independent vec4<f32> FMAs (acc = fma(acc, a, b)) and writes one result; dispatch e.g. 1024 workgroups x 256 threads. FLOPs = invocations x iters x 4 x 4 x 2. Also run an f16 variant if 'shader-f16' is enabled. Expected FP32: RTX 4090 50-70 TFLOPS, 4070 20-25, M2 3-3.3, M3 Max 12-14, iPhone 16 Pro 1.8-2.2, Adreno 750 2.5-4, Intel Xe 1.5-2.
 3. Timing: prefer timestamp-query when available (Chrome quantises to 100 microseconds, fine for 100 ms windows); otherwise performance.now() around submit + onSubmittedWorkDone (includes ~0.1-2 ms submission latency - negligible for >= 100 ms windows). performance.now resolution: 100 microseconds (Chrome, non-isolated), ~1 ms (Safari, Firefox; Firefox RFP 16.67-100 ms) - always measure windows >= 100 ms.
 4. Safety: keep any single submitted batch < 500 ms of GPU time (Windows TDR resets the GPU at 2 s, macOS/iOS kill long command buffers, Android drivers are fragile); scale down if the warm-up dispatch alone takes > 50 ms. Listen to device.lost (reason 'destroyed' vs 'unknown'); on loss, mark GPU 'unstable', skip remaining GPU tests, do not retry more than once. Wrap requestDevice in try/catch (OperationError on limits). Destroy buffers and call device.destroy() at the end to release VRAM. Handle document.visibilityState === 'hidden' (rAF/GPU throttled) by pausing.

C) Translating to a score:
 - Take measured GPU BW (B_gpu) and CPU aggregate estimate (B_cpu). If the GPU is identified with high confidence, compare B_gpu to 0.8 x spec peak: ratio < 0.6 => device is throttled/on battery/low-power adapter -> use measured for estimates and tell the user; ratio in 0.6-1.3 => use spec peak x eff factors from estimation_method (more accurate); ratio > 1.3 => identification wrong -> trust measured.
 - If unidentified (Safari/Firefox), peak_BW_est = B_gpu / 0.8 and plug into tok/s = eff x peak_BW_est / bytes_per_token; use measured TFLOPS for prefill and diffusion estimates.
 - Device tiers for a one-line summary (by effective BW for LLM decode): Tier 0 < 20 GB/s (old phones/iGPUs: tiny models only), Tier 1 20-70 (phones, base M1, iGPUs: 1-4B WELL, 7-8B SLOW), Tier 2 70-200 (M2-M5 base, Lunar Lake, mid GPUs with <= 8 GB: 7-8B WELL, 14B SLOW-to-WELL depending on RAM), Tier 3 200-500 (M Pro/Max, RTX 3060-4070 class: 14B WELL, 30B MoE WELL, 32B dense SLOW/WELL if fits), Tier 4 > 500 (RTX 4080/4090/5090, M Max/Ultra with 64 GB+: 32B WELL, 70B WELL only if it fits in fast memory).
 Pitfalls: thermal (phones lose 20-40% after ~60 s; our 5 s test measures 'burst' - apply 0.75 sustained factor on phones and fanless laptops), power-saver modes, the first WebGPU run includes shader compile, JIT warm-up for JS loops, GC pauses (preallocate), background tabs throttled to 1 Hz timers, and memory pressure causing iOS to reload the page.
pitfalls: navigator.deviceMemory changed in Chrome 147 (April 2026): desktop now reports 2/4/8/16/32 (cap 32), Android 1/2/4/8 (cap 8). Pre-147 Chromium (incl. many Samsung Internet/Opera/WebView builds) still caps at 8. Always interpret by browser major version; 32 and Android 8 are lower bounds, not values.
Firefox and Safari expose NO RAM signal at all (no deviceMemory, no performance.memory, no userAgentData). Macs and iPhones need screen-table inference or a user question.

Safari clamps hardwareConcurrency to 4 or 8 and reports WebGL renderer 'Apple GPU'; all iOS browsers (Chrome/Firefox/Edge on iOS) are WebKit and inherit these limits - do not trust 'CriOS'/'FxiOS' UA as Chromium/Gecko capability.
Safari WebGPU adapter.info only yields a vendor word ('apple', 'intelr', 'amd'); Firefox returns empty strings; only Chrome gives architecture. Never require adapter.info to be non-empty.

Firefox WEBGL_debug_renderer_info is deprecated and bucketed (', or similar'); the bucket may name an older GPU than the real one - treat it as a class, and it may disappear in a future Firefox release.

iPadOS and Apple Silicon Macs both report 'MacIntel' / 'Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7'; use maxTouchPoints > 1 for iPad and the Apple-Silicon checks (UA-CH architecture, Safari adapter.info.vendor, Firefox navigator.gpu presence) for Mac CPU type.

WebGPU availability is not device capability: Chrome on Linux only enables it for Intel Gen12+ (since 144); Firefox only on Windows and Apple Silicon macOS; Chrome Android needs Android 12+ and Adreno/Mali. A missing navigator.gpu on a Linux RTX 4090 box does not mean the machine is weak - fall back to WebGL renderer for native-verdict estimates.

Software adapters (SwiftShader, WARP, llvmpipe, 'Microsoft Basic Render Driver', isFallbackAdapter true) appear in VMs, RDP sessions and on blocklisted drivers; treat as 'GPU unknown' rather than 'weak GPU' and ask.
adapter.limits.maxBufferSize/maxStorageBufferBindingSize are allocation caps, not VRAM; do not display them as memory. They matter only as gates for in-browser runtimes.

Hybrid-GPU laptops: requestAdapter may return the iGPU even with powerPreference 'high-performance' (Windows per-app GPU preference overrides); WebGL may report the dGPU while WebGPU reports the iGPU. Report both and use the stronger for NATIVE verdicts, the WebGPU one for IN-BROWSER verdicts.

The page is likely not crossOriginIsolated (no COOP/COEP headers in a hosted single file/iframe): no SharedArrayBuffer, no WASM threads, coarse timers. Design benchmarks for single-thread and >= 100 ms windows, and don't claim in-browser multithreaded CPU inference works.

In a sandboxed iframe: navigator.storage.estimate can throw SecurityError, getBattery rejects (battery permissions policy 'self'), getHighEntropyValues can be blocked by the ch-ua-high-entropy-values permissions policy (Chrome 144+), and localStorage can throw. Wrap every call in try/catch and give each promise a timeout.

Privacy browsers/extensions (Brave farbling, Firefox resistFingerprinting, Tor, Mullvad) randomise or flatten values (e.g. hardwareConcurrency 2, WebGL 'Mozilla', WebGPU limits reset to defaults). Detect contradictions (e.g. 'RTX 4090' + 2 cores) and lower confidence.

Screen-size iPhone inference breaks with Display Zoom, landscape orientation (use min/max), Stage Manager/Split View on iPad, and identical panels across generations (402x874 = 16 Pro 8 GB, 17 8 GB, 17 Pro/18 Pro 12 GB). Report ranges and use lower-bound RAM for WELL.
Apple unified memory is not all usable by the GPU: Metal's recommended working set is ~66-75% of RAM, and macOS/other apps need 3-6 GB. A 16 GB Mac cannot comfortably run a 14 GB model.

iOS Safari tabs are killed (jetsam) far below device RAM (roughly 1.5-4 GB depending on model); in-browser verdicts on iPhone must be much more conservative than native-app verdicts (e.g. 8B Q4 native SLOW/WELL on 12 GB iPhone, but in-browser likely NO).

Benchmarks on battery, in low-power mode, or on a hot phone read 30-60% low; use getBattery where available and show a 'plug in / let it cool' note; apply a 0.75 sustained-performance factor on phones and fanless laptops.

Long GPU submissions can trigger Windows TDR (2 s) or device loss on mobile; cap each batch at < 500 ms and handle device.lost gracefully. Never run the benchmark automatically on page load (also avoids burning mobile data/battery and background-tab throttling).
MoE models: memory fit uses total params, speed uses active params; forgetting either produces wildly wrong verdicts (gpt-oss-120b needs ~65 GB but decodes like a 5B dense model).
Reasoning/thinking models emit many hidden tokens; a 10 tok/s device makes them feel slow - use a higher WELL threshold (>= 15 tok/s).
WebLLM q4f16 builds require 'shader-f16'; without it only q4f32 builds run (more memory, ~1.3-2x slower). Firefox and some Windows drivers lack shader-f16.

WASM memory32 caps the heap at 4 GiB (practically ~2-3.5 GB, ~1.5 GB on iOS); memory64 and relaxed-SIMD are not in Safari (preview only as of Safari 27), so CPU-only in-browser inference on Apple devices is limited to small models.
UA reduction: Chrome's UA always says 'Windows NT 10.0' and 'Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7' and Android 'K' model; use userAgentData.platformVersion (>= 13 => Windows 11) and model instead of UA regexes.
